response.explanation: OAuthLoginView uses pipeline.signature as the OAuth `state` and accepts any callback whose state equals it. In pipeline/base.py the signature is md5_text(*pipe_ids), computed from the pipeline's step class names. It is not random and not tied to the session, so every pipeline of this type has the same value, and an attacker can compute it. An attacker can send a victim, who has started a GitHub install in Sentry, a link to the setup callback with state=<known signature>&code=<attacker's own GitHub OAuth code>. The pipeline then stores the attacker's login as github_authenticated_user. GitHubInstallation.dispatch only compares that stored login to integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] for an Integration that already exists, so it passes when the attacker is the original installer.
response.title: OAuth state is a static md5 of pipeline class names, so the login-CSRF check does not bind the GitHub identity to the user
